It should apply an ordered set of properties: 264 265 ```mermaid 266 flowchart TD 267 A[Input / generated Case] --> B{Process survives?} 268 B -->|No| X1[Safety bug] 269 B -->|Yes| C{Reader accepted file?} 270 C --> D{Structural invariants hold?} 271 D -->|No| X2[Validation bug] 272 D --> E{Round-trip logical rows equal?} 273 E -->|No| X3[Semantic bug] 274 E --> F{Independent engines agree?} 275 F -->|No| X4[Interoperability disagreement] 276 F --> G{Optimized and reference paths agree?} 277 G -->|No| X5[Optimization bug] 278 G --> H[Pass] 279 ``` 280 281 For valid generated files, the strongest inexpensive oracle is usually **logical-table equality**, not encoded-byte equality. Two correct Parquet writers are free to choose different page boundaries, statistics encodings, compression streams and dictionary layouts. 282 283 For one implementation, use **metamorphic** comparisons: 284 285 - predicate pushdown enabled vs disabled; 286 - page-index pruning enabled vs disabled; 287 - row selection mask vs selector form; 288 - sync vs async reader; 289 - small vs large batches; 290 - projection before vs after filtering; 291 - dictionary vs plain writer where semantics permit; 292 - page V1 vs V2; 293 - statistics/Bloom filters present vs absent. 294 295 This directly operationalizes the `arrow-rs` issue #10747 recommendation to compare optimized behaviour with a simpler reference configuration. 296 297 For cross-implementation testing, use at least Arrow Rust, Arrow C++, and parquet-java. PyArrow is useful as a scripting frontend but does not provide an independent C++ parser because it is based on Arrow C++. 298 299 Parquity's `scan` design—compare reader observations without preselecting a reference reader—is particularly sensible when the standard permits multiple representations or when one implementation may itself be wrong. 300 301 ### Minimal Rust byte harness 302 303 The following is a practical starting point for `cargo-fuzz`. It is intentionally small: bytes that do not form a readable file are ordinary rejections; successful reads must not panic. 304 305 ```rust 306 #![no_main] 307 308 use libfuzzer_sys::fuzz_target; 309 use bytes::Bytes; 310 use parquet::arrow::arrow_reader::ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder; 311 312 fuzz_target!(|data: &[u8]| { 313 // Bytes implements the random-access input abstraction used by parquet-rs. 314 let input = Bytes::copy_from_slice(data); 315 316 let Ok(builder) = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(input) else { 317 return; 318 }; 319 320 let Ok(reader) = builder.with_batch_size(257).build() else { 321 return; 322 }; 323 324 for batch in reader { 325 match batch { 326 Ok(batch) => { 327 // Force materialization/use of basic structural information. 328 let _ = batch.num_rows(); 329 let _ = batch.num_columns(); 330 let _ = batch.schema(); 331 } 332 Err(_) => return, 333 } 334 } 335 }); 336 ``` 337 338 The current `parquet` crate supplies the relevant Arrow reader implementation and already has `proptest` in its dev environment; adding `cargo-fuzz` would complement, rather than replace, those semantic tests. 339 340 A production version should have several separate targets rather than one giant target: metadata-only parsing, page decoding, Arrow conversion, full-file reads, encrypted reads, page-index reads and writer→reader round trips. This keeps executions fast and makes coverage deficiencies diagnosable. 341 342 A recommended `fuzz/Cargo.toml` skeleton is: 343 344 ```toml 345 [package] 346 name = "parquet-fuzz" 347 version = "0.0.0" 348 publish = false 349 edition = "2024" 350 351 [package.metadata] 352 cargo-fuzz = true 353 354 [dependencies] 355 libfuzzer-sys = "0.4" 356 bytes = "1" 357 358 [dependencies.parquet] 359 path = "../parquet" 360 features = ["arrow", "crc", "encryption"] 361 362 [[bin]] 363 name = "read_file" 364 path = "fuzz_targets/read_file.rs" 365 test = false 366 doc = false 367 bench = false 368 ``` 369 370 ### Minimal C++ libFuzzer harness 371 372 This is a simplified stand-alone equivalent of the class of work performed by Arrow's own richer fuzz target: 373 374 ```cpp 375 #include 376 #include 377 #include 378 379 #include 380 #include 381 #include 382 #include 383 384 extern "C" int LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput(const uint8_t* data, size_t size) { 385 auto buffer = std::make_shared(data, size); 386 auto input = std::make_shared(buffer); 387 388 std::unique_ptr reader; 389 auto status = 390 parquet::arrow::OpenFile(input, arrow::default_memory_pool(), &reader); 391 392 if (!status.ok()) { 393 return 0; // malformed input is expected 394 } 395 396 std::shared_ptr table; 397 status = reader->ReadTable(&table); 398 399 if (status.ok()) { 400 // A successful parse should produce a structurally valid Arrow table. 401 auto validation = table->ValidateFull(); 402 if (!validation.ok()) { 403 __builtin_trap(); 404 } 405 } 406 407 return 0; 408 } 409 ``` 410 411 The important design principle is the final validation step: “reader returned success” is not enough. Arrow's current fuzzing direction similarly treats structural validation as a meaningful oracle, and recent C++ bugs demonstrate that sanitizer-backed decode paths remain productive. 412 413 ### Schema-aware Rust property harness 414 415 A higher-value semantic test generates **valid** schemas and values, writes them, and reads them through several modes. 416 417 ```rust 418 proptest! { 419 #[test] 420 fn parquet_roundtrip(case in arbitrary_parquet_case()) { 421 let bytes = write_case( 422 &case.schema, 423 &case.rows, 424 &case.writer_properties, 425 )?; 426 427 let reference = read_case( 428 &bytes, 429 ReadConfig { 430 page_index: false, 431 predicate_cache: false, 432 row_selection: RowSelectionMode::Selectors, 433 batch_size: 1024, 434 }, 435 )?; 436 437 for config in generated_read_configs(&case) { 438 let actual = read_case(&bytes, config)?; 439 440 prop_assert_eq!( 441 normalize(actual), 442 normalize(reference) 443 ); 444 } 445 } 446 } 447 ``` 448 449 The critical part is `arbitrary_parquet_case()`. It should be biased toward **boundaries and feature interactions**, not uniformly random schemas. The Rust issue #10747 gives concrete high-yield dimensions: sparse single-row selections, selections crossing page boundaries, cache sizes around eviction thresholds, projections overlapping predicate columns and page sizes that interact awkwardly with batch boundaries. 450 451 ### Cross-engine harness 452 453 A useful independent test protocol is: 454 455 ```text 456 Case(schema, rows, writer_options) 457 | 458 +--> arrow-rs writer ------+ 459 +--> Arrow C++ writer -----+--> each .parquet file 460 +--> parquet-java writer --+ 461 | 462 +-------------------+-------------------+ 463 v v v 464 arrow-rs reader Arrow C++ reader parquet-java reader 465 | | | 466 +--------- normalize logical result ---+ 467 | 468 compare all 469 ``` 470 471 Every failure artifact should retain: 472 473 ```json 474 { 475 "schema": "... canonical representation ...", 476 "logical_rows": "...", 477 "writer": "arrow-rs", 478 "writer_version": "60.1.0", 479 "writer_options": { 480 "page_version": "V2", 481 "compression": "zstd", 482 "dictionary": true, 483 "page_index": true 484 }, 485 "readers": { 486 "arrow-rs": "... normalized result or error ...", 487 "arrow-cpp": "...", 488 "parquet-java": "..." 489 }, 490 "input_sha256": "...", 491 "minimized_from": "..." 492 } 493 ``` 494 495 Parquity already embodies much of this Case-oriented philosophy and should be evaluated before inventing another outer orchestration layer. 496 497 ## CI, coverage and performance measurement 498 499 ### Existing continuous-fuzzing signal 500 501 The latest OSS-Fuzz Fuzz Introspector snapshot found during this research is dated 9 September 2026. It reports approximately **12.53%** project-source coverage for `parquet-arrow-fuzz` and **3.37%** for `parquet-encoding-fuzz`; the encoding fuzz target's coverage job also recorded a memory-limit problem at roughly 2.28 GB against a 2 GB limit. These percentages are Fuzz Introspector's target-level project coverage, not “12.53% of every Parquet semantic state” and not a quality score. 502 503 That distinction is important. Low aggregate source coverage can coexist with good coverage of the intended decoder, while high line coverage can still miss cross-feature combinations such as the Rust predicate-cache failure. Therefore measure both **code coverage** and **semantic coverage**. 504 505 For code-level measurements, track: 506 507 - functions/lines/edges reached per target; 508 - sanitizer-specific corpus findings; 509 - executions/second and median input size; 510 - corpus size after minimization; 511 - coverage delta when adding a generator or mutator; 512 - time-to-first-hit for a fixed benchmark set. 513 514 For semantic coverage, track a matrix such as: 515 516 ```text 517 Physical type × Logical type 518 Encoding × DataPage version 519 Compression codec × dictionary on/off 520 Required/optional/repeated × nesting depth 521 Null density × run-length distribution 522 Page size × batch size 523 Row-group size × projection width 524 Page index × predicate type 525 Bloom filter × predicate selectivity 526 CRC × valid/corrupt checksum 527 Encryption × footer/column-key mode 528 Reader optimisation × selection representation 529 ``` 530 531 The second matrix would have exposed the exact kind of cross-product hole documented by `arrow-rs` #10747. 532 533 ### Recommended pull-request CI for Rust 534 535 A reasonable GitHub Actions pattern is to use bounded fuzzing on every relevant PR and leave indefinite campaigns to OSS-Fuzz: 536 537 ```yaml 538 name: parquet-fuzz-smoke 539 540 on: 541 pull_request: 542 paths: 543 - "parquet/**" 544 - "fuzz/**" 545 546 jobs: 547 fuzz: 548 runs-on: ubuntu-latest 549 strategy: 550 matrix: 551 target: 552 - read_metadata 553 - read_file 554 - decode_pages 555 - roundtrip 556 steps: 557 - uses: actions/checkout@v4 558 with: 559 submodules: recursive 560 561 - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly 562 563 - run: cargo install cargo-fuzz 564 565 - name: Fuzz target 566 run: | 567 cargo fuzz run "${{ matrix.target }}" \ 568 corpus/"${{ matrix.target }}" \ 569 -- -max_total_time=120 -timeout=5 570 571 - name: Replay regression corpus 572 run: | 573 cargo test -p parquet 574 ``` 575 576 This is a **recommended configuration**, not evidence of the current `arrow-rs` CI. The existing Rust repository does already use the shared Parquet test-data ecosystem and carries property/benchmark dependencies, while the current open issue explicitly calls for broader fuzz-state coverage. 577 578 ### Recommended OSS-Fuzz Rust project structure 579 580 OSS-Fuzz supports Rust as a language and documents the same project model—`project.yaml`, Dockerfile and `build.sh`—used for C/C++ integrations. 581 582 A Rust Parquet integration should initially expose distinct targets: 583 584 ```text 585 parquet-rs-metadata-fuzz 586 parquet-rs-page-fuzz 587 parquet-rs-arrow-reader-fuzz 588 parquet-rs-async-reader-fuzz 589 parquet-rs-encryption-fuzz 590 parquet-rs-roundtrip-fuzz 591 parquet-rs-page-index-fuzz 592 ``` 593 594 Separating them matters because a single full-file target tends to spend most of its budget in shallow structural parsing and makes it difficult to distinguish coverage progress in codecs, page indexes, Arrow conversion and selection logic. 595 596 OSS-Fuzz's own project guide strongly recommends seed corpora and supports target-specific dictionaries. For Parquet, a dictionary should include magic bytes and useful encoded tokens only where it genuinely helps; structure-aware generation is likely more valuable than a huge byte dictionary because much of the format's complexity lies in dependent length fields and Thrift metadata. 597 598 ### Benchmark methodology 599 600 No comparable public benchmark was found that establishes “fuzzer A is X% better than fuzzer B for current Arrow Parquet” under controlled identical hardware and corpora. The available current quantitative source is Fuzz Introspector's target coverage, which should be treated as an operational indicator rather than a comparative research benchmark. 601 602 A proper benchmark should therefore be created. Use a fixed commit and sanitizer build and run 20–30 independent repetitions per engine/mutator because fuzzing outcomes are stochastic. Measure: 603 604 ```text 605 time to each known seeded bug 606 edge coverage over time 607 semantic-cell coverage over time 608 unique sanitizer failures 609 unique semantic disagreements 610 executions per second 611 median and p95 RSS 612 corpus bytes / unique coverage edge 613 minimization effectiveness 614 ``` 615 616 The benchmark suite should contain historical bugs from C++ and Rust, including a reconstruction of CVE-2019-12410, recent OSS-Fuzz decoding failures and the 2026 Rust feature-interaction regressions. The historical standalone C++ changelog gives additional candidate bugs for ground-truth replay. 617 618 For an external comparison point, DuckDB itself has a current OSS-Fuzz `parquet_fuzz_test` visible in Fuzz Introspector, demonstrating that Parquet readers outside Apache can be additional independent fuzz targets/oracles rather than merely consumers. 619 620 ## Gaps and recommended research programme 621 622 ### The main gaps 623 624 **Rust lacks the same visible continuous fuzzing depth as C++.** The official Rust crate clearly has property/randomized testing infrastructure, and historical `parquet-rs` had fuzzing code, but the present public evidence reviewed here does not show a first-class Rust Parquet OSS-Fuzz campaign equivalent to Arrow C++. Given OSS-Fuzz's explicit Rust support, that is the clearest infrastructure opportunity. 625 626 **Feature combinations are under-modelled.** The 2026 Rust bug is direct evidence that individually well-tested features can fail only in combination. Randomly sampling all dimensions uniformly will not solve this efficiently because the cross-product is enormous. Pairwise/t-wise combinatorial generation should therefore sit alongside randomized property testing. 627 628 **Same-lineage differential testing can create false confidence.** PyArrow and Arrow C++ are one implementation family, and historical `parquet-cpp` is the predecessor of current Arrow C++ rather than an independent modern implementation. The core differential set should include parquet-java and at least one additional independent engine. 629 630 **The oracle needs to test values, not merely acceptance or row counts.** The Rust maintainers themselves identify row-count-only assertions as too weak and suggest comparing complete results against a reference configuration. 631 632 **Structural mutation remains a high-value frontier.** Raw fuzzing is excellent for parser robustness, but Parquet's dependent metadata and offsets make deep valid-state exploration expensive. FuzzBerg and FormatFuzzer show two viable models—file-format-specific stitching and generated grammar-aware mutators, respectively. 633 634 **Coverage measurement is too code-centric.** The current OSS-Fuzz numbers are useful, but they cannot tell whether every meaningful encoding/logical-type/page-index/encryption combination has been explored. 635 636 ### Recommended programme 637 638 The first workstream should establish **one canonical semantic generator**, preferably in a language-neutral serialized form. It should generate an Arrow-like logical schema, rows and option matrix. Writers then turn that Case into Parquet, and all readers normalize results back into the same logical representation. Parquity provides a practical existing reference design for Case generation and reduction. 639 640 The second workstream should build **three tiers of mutation**: raw coverage-guided bytes, structure-preserving Parquet mutation and semantic Case mutation. The structure layer should parse the footer and page metadata before choosing mutation sites; the semantic layer should mutate logical values and options and then regenerate a valid file. FormatFuzzer's parse/generate/mutate architecture is a useful academic blueprint. 641 642 The third should be **differential execution across implementation families**: 643 644 ```mermaid 645 flowchart LR 646 C[Generated Case] 647 WR[arrow-rs writer] 648 WC[Arrow C++ writer] 649 WJ[parquet-java writer] 650 651 RR[arrow-rs reader] 652 RC[Arrow C++ reader] 653 RJ[parquet-java reader] 654 RD[Independent DB reader] 655 656 N[Canonical logical normalization] 657 M{Agreement?} 658 R[Reduce Case and file] 659 660 C --> WR 661 C --> WC 662 C --> WJ 663 664 WR --> RR 665 WR --> RC 666 WR --> RJ 667 WC --> RR 668 WC --> RC 669 WC --> RJ 670 WJ --> RR 671 WJ --> RC 672 WJ --> RJ 673 674 WR --> RD 675 WC --> RD 676 WJ --> RD 677 678 RR --> N 679 RC --> N 680 RJ --> N 681 RD --> N 682 N --> M 683 M -->|No| R 684 ``` 685 686 The fourth workstream should create a **Parquet semantic-coverage ledger**. Every CI or fuzz run should report which dimensions and cross-products were observed. That converts “we fuzz Parquet” into an auditable statement such as “all physical/logical type pairs, every supported encoding, V1/V2 pages, all compression codecs, encrypted/plain footers, page indexes, Bloom filters and every reader selection policy were exercised this week.” 687 688 The fifth should create a **ground-truth bug benchmark**. Populate it with historical issues from the C++ changelog, CVE-2019-12410, recent OSS-Fuzz findings and current Rust regressions. A new mutator or generator should have to demonstrate faster or more reliable discovery of those hidden known bugs before being adopted. 689 690 The sixth should make **regression promotion automatic**: every minimized OSS-Fuzz crash, panic or differential disagreement becomes an immutable test input plus a machine-readable description of the expected behaviour. `apache/parquet-testing` is the natural shared destination for genuinely cross-implementation fixtures; implementation-specific minimized cases can remain in each repository. The shared repository already exists precisely for compatibility and regression testing. 691 692 Finally, treat **resource exhaustion as correctness/security**, not noise. Parquet exposes attacker-controlled nesting, lengths, compressed sizes, page counts and metadata. Every harness should have explicit limits for CPU, RSS, recursion depth and output amplification; OOM and timeout findings should be triaged separately from malformed-input rejections. The fact that the current Fuzz Introspector run itself records a memory-limit failure for the encoding target is a useful reminder that memory behaviour needs explicit measurement. 693 694 The resulting target state is stronger than conventional fuzzing: malformed bytes exercise parser safety; generated valid files exercise deep semantics; independent engines identify interoperability failures; metamorphic configurations isolate optimisation bugs; and every finding feeds a permanently growing corpus. That combination is the most likely route to finding the next class of Parquet defects that ordinary unit tests—and byte fuzzers alone—will miss.

.DEFAULT_GOAL := help
MAKEFLAGS += --no-print-directory

LIB_DIR := zig-parquet
CLI_DIR := cli
EXAMPLES_DIR := $(LIB_DIR)/examples

# Toolchain: make <target> ZIG=/path/to/zig   (0.16.x and 0.17.x are supported)
ZIG ?= zig
ZIG_VERSION := $(shell $(ZIG) version)
# Non-0.16 toolchains use their own local cache under <repo>/.zig17 (gitignored).
# $(1) = path from the recipe's working directory back to the repo root.
zcache = $(if $(filter 0.16.%,$(ZIG_VERSION)),,--cache-dir $(1)/.zig17/cache)

# Parameterize builds: `make lib CODECS=c-brotli OPT=ReleaseSmall`
CODECS ?=
OPT ?=
NAME ?=
CODEC_FLAG := $(if $(CODECS),-Dcodecs=$(CODECS))
OPT_FLAG := $(if $(OPT),-Doptimize=$(OPT))

.PHONY: help
help:
	@echo "Run from repo root — never cd into subdirs."
	@echo ""
	@echo "Toolchain: ZIG=<path to zig> (default: zig on PATH; 0.16.x and 0.17.x supported)"
	@echo ""
	@echo "Targets (all accept CODECS=<spec> OPT=<ReleaseSmall|ReleaseFast|...> ZIG=<zig>):"
	@echo "  make build             Build library + CLI"
	@echo "  make lib               Build library (honors CODECS, OPT)"
	@echo "  make cli               Build pqi CLI (honors CODECS, OPT)"
	@echo "  make test              Library + CLI tests (honors CODECS, OPT)"
	@echo "  make test-lib          Library tests only (honors CODECS, OPT)"
	@echo "  make test-cli          CLI tests only (honors CODECS, OPT)"
	@echo "  make example NAME=...  Build an example (honors CODECS, OPT)"
	@echo "  make wasm              Verify WASM targets compile and link (no C codecs unless CODECS is set)"
	@echo "  make bench [ROWS=n]    Run the benchmark harness (ReleaseFast, zig-only codecs by default)"
	@echo "  make bench-rust [ROWS=n]  Same scenarios with the Rust parquet crate (bench/rust)"
	@echo "  make bench-wasm        Build zig-out/bin/zpbench.wasm for the JS benchmarks in bench/js"
	@echo "  make bench-js-browsers [ROWS=n]  zig-parquet WASM vs hyparquet and parquet-wasm in Chrome and Firefox"
	@echo "  make bench-js-workerd [ROWS=n]   The same in workerd"
	@echo "  make validate-wild     Validate pqi against wild files (failures only)"
	@echo "  make validate-wild-all Validate pqi against wild files (show all)"
	@echo "  make fmt               zig fmt across sources (requires ZIG=<0.16 zig>)"
	@echo "  make clean             Remove .zig-cache and zig-out everywhere"
	@echo ""
	@echo "Examples:"
	@echo "  make test CODECS=zig-only"
	@echo "  make test CODECS=c-zstd,zstd"
	@echo "  make lib CODECS=c-brotli OPT=ReleaseSmall"
	@echo "  make lib CODECS=none OPT=ReleaseSmall"
	@echo "  make example NAME=basic"
	@echo "  make example NAME=wasm_demo OPT=ReleaseSmall"
	@echo "  make test-lib CODECS=zig-only ZIG=C:/tools/zig-0.16.0/zig.exe"
	@echo ""
	@echo "Examples (NAME=): basic, gen-power-grid, large_file,"
	@echo "                  wasm_demo, wasm_freestanding"
	@echo ""
	@echo "CODECS values: all (default), none, zig-only, c-only,"
	@echo "  or comma list of: zstd|snappy|gzip|lz4|brotli (Zig)"
	@echo "                    c-zstd|c-snappy|c-gzip|c-lz4|c-brotli (C/C++)"

.PHONY: build
build: lib cli

.PHONY: lib
lib:
	cd $(LIB_DIR) && $(ZIG) build $(call zcache,..) $(CODEC_FLAG) $(OPT_FLAG)

.PHONY: cli
cli:
	cd $(CLI_DIR) && $(ZIG) build $(call zcache,..) $(CODEC_FLAG) $(OPT_FLAG)

.PHONY: test
test: test-lib test-cli

.PHONY: test-lib
test-lib:
	cd $(LIB_DIR) && $(ZIG) build test $(call zcache,..) $(CODEC_FLAG) $(OPT_FLAG)

.PHONY: test-cli
test-cli:
	cd $(CLI_DIR) && $(ZIG) build test $(call zcache,..) $(CODEC_FLAG) $(OPT_FLAG)

.PHONY: example
example:
	@test -n "$(NAME)" || { echo "usage: make example NAME=<basic|gen-power-grid|large_file|wasm_demo|wasm_freestanding>"; exit 1; }
	@test -d $(EXAMPLES_DIR)/$(NAME) || { echo "no such example: $(NAME)"; ls $(EXAMPLES_DIR); exit 1; }
	cd $(EXAMPLES_DIR)/$(NAME) && $(ZIG) build $(call zcache,../../..) $(CODEC_FLAG) $(OPT_FLAG)

.PHONY: wasm
wasm:
	cd $(LIB_DIR) && $(ZIG) build wasm-smoke $(call zcache,..) $(if $(CODECS),$(CODEC_FLAG),-Dcodecs=none)

.PHONY: bench
bench:
	cd $(LIB_DIR) && $(ZIG) build bench $(call zcache,..) -Dcodecs=$(or $(CODECS),zig-only) -Doptimize=ReleaseFast $(if $(ROWS),-- $(ROWS))

.PHONY: bench-wasm
bench-wasm:
	cd $(LIB_DIR) && $(ZIG) build bench-wasm $(call zcache,..) -Dcodecs=none -Doptimize=$(or $(OPT),ReleaseFast)

.PHONY: bench-rust
bench-rust:
	cd bench/rust && cargo run --release $(if $(ROWS),-- $(ROWS))

.PHONY: bench-js-browsers bench-js-workerd
bench-js-browsers: bench-wasm
	cd bench/js && (test -d node_modules || npm ci) && node run-browsers.mjs $(or $(ROWS),1000000)

bench-js-workerd: bench-wasm
	cd bench/js && (test -d node_modules || npm ci) && node run-workerd.mjs $(or $(ROWS),1000000)

.PHONY: validate-wild
validate-wild: cli
	cd $(CLI_DIR) && ./validate-wild.sh

.PHONY: validate-wild-all
validate-wild-all: cli
	cd $(CLI_DIR) && ./validate-wild.sh --all

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7

      - uses: denoland/setup-deno@v2

      - name: Generate test files
        working-directory: test-files-arrow
        run: uv run python generate.py

      - name: Build library
        working-directory: zig-parquet
        run: zig build

      - name: Run tests
        working-directory: zig-parquet
        run: zig build test

      - name: WASM smoke test
        working-directory: zig-parquet
        run: zig build wasm-smoke

      - name: Build examples
        run: |
          cd zig-parquet/examples/basic && zig build
          cd ../../examples/large_file && zig build
          cd ../../examples/gen-power-grid && zig build
          cd ../../examples/wasm_demo && zig build
          cd ../../examples/wasm_freestanding && zig build

#!/bin/bash
#
# Validate all parquet files in test-files-wild directory
# Usage: ./validate-wild.sh [--all] [--verbose] [directory]
#
# Options:
#   --all, -a      Show all files (default: only unexpected results)
#   --verbose, -v  Show detailed output for each file
#
# Exit codes:
#   0 - All results match expectations
#   1 - Regressions or unexpected results detected
#

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PROJECT_ROOT="$(dirname "$SCRIPT_DIR")"
WILD_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/test-files-wild"
PQ_BIN="$SCRIPT_DIR/zig-out/bin/pqi"
EXPECTED_FAILURES="$WILD_DIR/expected-failures.txt"

VERBOSE=false
SHOW_ALL=false
for arg in "$@"; do
    case "$arg" in
        --verbose|-v) VERBOSE=true ;;
        --all|-a) SHOW_ALL=true ;;
        -*) echo "Unknown option: $arg"; exit 1 ;;
        *) WILD_DIR="$arg" ;;
    esac
done

RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[0;33m'
CYAN='\033[0;36m'
NC='\033[0m'

# Returns 0 if the file is in expected-failures.txt, 1 otherwise.
# Prints the expected error pattern on match.
is_expected_failure() {
    local rel_path="$1"
    if [[ -f "$EXPECTED_FAILURES" ]]; then
        local match
        match=$(grep -v '^#' "$EXPECTED_FAILURES" | grep -v '^$' | awk -v p="$rel_path" '$1 == p {print $2; exit}')
        if [[ -n "$match" ]]; then
            echo "$match"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    return 1
}

extract_error() {
    local output="$1"
    local err=""
    err=$(echo "$output" | grep -oE "FAILED \([A-Za-z]+\)" | head -1 || true)
    if [[ -z "$err" ]]; then
        err=$(echo "$output" | grep -oE "panic: [^$]+" | head -1 | cut -c1-60 || true)

content.content:
# Fuzzing zarrow

zarrow's fuzzing follows Apache Arrow C++'s setup: one entry point per untrusted-input reader,
every decoded array goes through `validateFull`, a returned error is a pass, and a crash, hang,
leak or allocation blow-up is a bug. Seeds come from
[apache/arrow-testing](https://github.com/apache/arrow-testing) and from zarrow's own writers;
every fixed bug leaves its reproducer in `fuzz/corpus/` so CI replays it forever.

## Pieces

| Piece | What it does |
|---|---|
| `fuzz/fuzz.zig` | The harness: `runOne(target, allocator, bytes)` for every target, the replay / mutation CLI, seed generation, and `std.testing.fuzz` tests. |
| `tools/fuzz.py` | Supervisor: runs the harness in a loop, classifies crashes, saves and dedupes reproducers. |
| `tools/fuzz_triage.py` | Markdown report of a fuzz output dir. |
| `tools/fuzz_import_seeds.py` | Copies arrow-testing IPC reproducers and integration fixtures into the corpus. |
| `fuzz/corpus/<dir>/` | Committed seeds (`at-*` from arrow-testing, `gen-*` from `fuzz-gen-seeds`, `regress-*` fixed findings). |

Targets (`zig build fuzz -- <target> ...`):

| Target | Input bytes are | Corpus dir |
|---|---|---|
| `ipc-stream` | an IPC stream for `IpcStreamReader.init` (tensor streams via `nextTensorLikeMessage`) | `ipc-stream` |
| `ipc-stream-zero-copy` | the same, through `IpcStreamReader.initZeroCopy` | `ipc-stream` |
| `ipc-file` | an IPC file for `IpcFileReader` (batches, tensors, sparse tensors) | `ipc-file` |
| `array-layout` | a recipe for a hand-built `ArrayData` tree (type, lengths, buffers, children); `validateLayout`, then `validateFull`, then compute | `array-layout` |
| `compute` | an IPC stream; every column that passes `validateFull` goes through slice / take / filter / concat with indices derived from the input, and every result must pass `validateFull` with the expected length | `ipc-stream` |
| `c-abi` | a recipe for `ArrowSchema` / `ArrowArray` trees imported with `importSchemaFromC` / `importArrayFromC`; an accepted array goes through compute like above, then is exported and re-imported | `c-abi` |

What counts as a finding (the harness panics, the supervisor saves the input):

- any panic: safety checks in Debug / ReleaseSafe are our sanitizer (bounds, overflow, invalid
  enum, unreachable, use of a released ref usually segfaults on the 0xaa fill);
- `fuzz-leak`: bytes still allocated after one input (a counting allocator wraps every input);
- `fuzz-oom`: more than `--alloc-cap` live bytes (default 256 MiB) for one input of at most
  1 MiB, i.e. an allocation sized by an unchecked length;
- `fuzz-invariant`: a kernel turned a valid array into an invalid one or the wrong length;
- `fuzz-hang`: one input running longer than `--timeout` seconds (default 10; exit code 77);
- RSS over `--rss-mb` (supervisor, default 2048).

## Run a campaign

```sh
# 10 minutes per target, all targets; Debug by default, --optimize ReleaseSafe is ~5x faster.
python tools/fuzz.py --out .fuzz-out run --targets all --seconds 600
# one target, faster build
python tools/fuzz.py --optimize ReleaseSafe --out .fuzz-out run --targets ipc-file --seconds 300
# replay a directory one process per file (e.g. new arrow-testing reproducers)
python tools/fuzz.py --out .fuzz-out replay --target ipc-stream path/to/dir
```

The supervisor builds `zig build fuzz-install` (zig-out/bin/zarrow-fuzz), then runs
`zarrow-fuzz <target> run <chunk>s --corpus fuzz/corpus/<dir> --out .fuzz-out/<target>` in
chunks. The harness first runs every corpus input once, then mutates (bit/byte flips, arithmetic,
interesting integers, insert / erase / copy, splices between corpus entries, Arrow tokens such as
`ARROW1`, the 0xFFFFFFFF continuation marker and end-of-stream). Without coverage feedback an
input joins the corpus when it produces a new signature: error name, batch count, `validateFull`
error and the set of decoded type ids. Growth goes to `.fuzz-out/<target>/corpus/` and is
reloaded by the next chunk.

Before each execution the harness writes the input to `.fuzz-out/<target>/current.bin`, so a
crash always leaves its reproducer. The supervisor then saves `<sha1-16>.bin` + `.txt` (stack
trace) per unique signature (kind + panic message + top three stack frames), keeps the smallest
input, counts duplicates in `index.json` and marks the input in `skip/` so the restarted harness
does not crash on it again while loading the corpus.

The harness can be used directly too:

```sh
zig build fuzz -- ipc-stream replay fuzz/corpus/ipc-stream            # every file, one process
zig build fuzz -- compute run 100000 --corpus fuzz/corpus/ipc-stream --out .fuzz-out/compute --seed 1
```

## Read the triage report

```sh
python tools/fuzz_triage.py .fuzz-out > triage.md
```

Per target, one section per signature: kind and count, the panic message, the smallest
reproducer and its trace file, the first ten non-std stack frames, and the first frame inside
`src/` as the suggested place to start. For a leak the frames are the error return trace of the
failing path (the stack at the leak check is just the harness): the first `src/` frame is where
the error started, the leak is in a caller's cleanup on that path.

## Reproduce one crash

```sh
zig build fuzz -- ipc-stream replay .fuzz-out/ipc-stream/0123456789abcdef.bin
```

Under a debugger, run the installed harness with the same arguments:

```sh
zig build fuzz-install
gdb --args zig-out/bin/zarrow-fuzz ipc-stream replay crash.bin    # or lldb -- ...
# Windows: devenv /debugexe zig-out\bin\zarrow-fuzz.exe ipc-stream replay crash.bin (or WinDbg)
```

Check whether a bounds panic is a memory-safety bug in release builds by replaying with
`zig build fuzz -Doptimize=ReleaseFast -- <target> replay <file>`: there the check is gone and the
read is out of bounds (it may or may not fault).

## Fix it

1. Fix the root cause at the trust boundary, in the shared function every caller goes through:
   the IPC bytes and the C ABI structs are untrusted, everything decoded from them must be
   validated before it is used. For example: verify a flatbuffer once before any generated
   unpacker reads it, instead of guarding each accessor; never let a length prefix size an
   allocation before the bytes exist; bound child offsets by what every consumer indexes.
2. Never make a finding go away by loosening validation, catching the panic, raising the caps,
   or special-casing the reproducer. A rejected input must return an error.
3. Error paths free what they allocated: put one `errdefer` at the scope that owns the resource;
   an `errdefer` inside an `if` block stops covering it when the block ends.
4. Add the regression seed: copy the reproducer to `fuzz/corpus/<corpus dir>/regress-<first 8
   hex of its name>.bin` (the arrow-testing convention: reproducers stay in the corpus). Where a
   unit test states the rule more clearly, add one next to the fix too.
5. Re-run on both compilers:

```sh
zig build test && zig build fuzz-corpus
C:\path\to\zig-0.16\zig.exe build test --cache-dir .zig-cache16    # or zig-0.16 on PATH
zig-0.16 build fuzz-corpus --cache-dir .zig-cache16
python tools/fuzz.py --out .fuzz-out run --targets <target> --seconds 300
```

If an input is valid Arrow that zarrow rejects (an Arrow writer produced it), that is a
compatibility gap, not a fuzz bug: open an issue, do not add it as a regression seed that
expects rejection.

## Coverage-guided fuzzing (Zig's built-in fuzzer)

Each target is also a `std.testing.fuzz` test in `fuzz/fuzz.zig`. Plain `zig build test` runs
each once on its embedded seed and on empty input. On Linux the real coverage-guided engine runs
headless with an iteration limit:

```sh
zig build fuzz-test --fuzz=1M                        # Zig 0.17 (Debug works)
zig build fuzz-test --fuzz=1M -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe # Zig 0.16: Debug fuzz builds hit a test-runner compile error
zig build fuzz-test --fuzz                           # no limit: opens the web UI
```

Limitations: `--fuzz` is not implemented on Windows (both 0.16 and 0.17 print
`--fuzz not yet implemented for windows`); a failing input is reported by the fuzzer but is not
written as a file by zarrow's tooling, so reproduce it through the portable harness once found.

## Seeds

```sh
python -I tools/fuzz_import_seeds.py <arrow-testing checkout>   # at-* files + NOTICE
zig build fuzz-gen-seeds                                        # gen-* files
```

`fuzz_import_seeds.py` copies arrow-testing `data/arrow-ipc-stream`, `data/arrow-ipc-file`,
`data/arrow-ipc-tensor-stream` and a selection of `integration/` fixtures (Arrow 0.14.1, 1.0.0
big-endian, 2.0.0 compression, 4.0.0 shared dictionaries, C++ 21) up to 32 KiB each, deduped by
content hash; the `NOTICE` in each corpus dir records origin, revision and the Apache-2.0
license. `fuzz-gen-seeds` re-encodes every valid stream in the corpus with zarrow's writers
(plain, lz4, zstd; stream and file; plus a sliced copy of each batch) so mutations start from
zarrow-produced inputs for every type the readers support. Keep the committed corpus under about
2 MB.

## CI

- `ci.yml` (every push / PR): `zig build fuzz-corpus` replays the committed corpus through every
  target, then a 20-second mutation smoke per target; `zig build test` runs the
  `std.testing.fuzz` tests once on all OS / compiler lanes.
- `nightly-fuzz.yml`: 10 minutes per target (ReleaseSafe) with crash artifacts and the triage
  report in the job summary, plus an informational `zig build fuzz-test --fuzz=2M` job.

# Interop Test Files

These Parquet files are **written by zig-parquet** (not PyArrow) during `zig build test`.
They are then read and validated by `../test_interop.py` using PyArrow to confirm
cross-implementation compatibility.

Do not edit these files manually — they are regenerated on every test run.
"""Verify that zig-parquet-written files are readable by PyArrow."""

import struct
from datetime import date, datetime, time, timezone
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

INTEROP_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "interop"


def interop_path(name: str) -> Path:
    path = INTEROP_DIR / name
    if not path.exists():
        pytest.skip(f"{path} not found — run 'zig build test' first")
    return path


def _as_str(v):
    return v.decode("utf-8") if isinstance(v, bytes) else v


def _to_bytes(v):
    if v is None:
        return None
    return v.bytes if hasattr(v, "bytes") else bytes(v)


def _normalize_ts(ts):
    if ts is None:
        return None
    if hasattr(ts, "astimezone") and ts.tzinfo is None:
        return ts.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    return ts


def _decode_interval(raw):
    if raw is None:
        return None
    b = bytes(raw)
    months = struct.unpack_from("<I", b, 0)[0]
    days = struct.unpack_from("<I", b, 4)[0]
    millis = struct.unpack_from("<I", b, 8)[0]
    return (months, days, millis)


def _wkb_point_xy(raw):
    x = struct.unpack_from("<d", raw, 5)[0]
    y = struct.unpack_from("<d", raw, 13)[0]
    return x, y

3:A pure Zig Parquet library. All five compression codecs. No C dependencies. Runs anywhere.
13:Pure Zig, all five compression codecs, no C compiler required. Measured with `ReleaseSmall`.
18:| WASM (brotli-compressed) | 199 KB |
20:The 1,365 KB figure includes all five Zig codecs. Per-codec cost (on top of a 992 KB codec-less baseline) ranges from 89 KB for lz4 to 254 KB for brotli — use `-Dcodecs=` to pick a subset. See [COMPRESSION.md](COMPRESSION.md) for the full breakdown.
25:- **Full Read/Write Support** - Read and write Parquet files with all physical and logical types
26:- **All Standard Encodings** - PLAIN, RLE, DICTIONARY, DELTA_BINARY_PACKED, DELTA_LENGTH_BYTE_ARRAY, DELTA_BYTE_ARRAY, BYTE_STREAM_SPLIT
27:- **Nested Types** - Lists, structs, maps, and arbitrary nesting depth
28:- **Compression** - zstd, gzip, snappy, lz4, brotli — pure Zig by default, no C/C++ required; C backends available as opt-in via `-Dcodecs=c-only`
29:- **Logical Types** - STRING, DATE, TIME, TIMESTAMP (millis/micros/nanos), DECIMAL, UUID, INT annotations, FLOAT16, ENUM, JSON, BSON, INTERVAL, GEOMETRY, GEOGRAPHY
33:- **Page Index** - Read and write OffsetIndex + ColumnIndex; `readRowsFiltered` skips pages whose min/max can't match a predicate, reading only needed byte ranges
34:- **Page-Level CRC Checksums** - Written by default, validated on read
36:- **DataPage V1 and V2** - Read both page formats; write uses V1
39:- **C ABI with Arrow C Data Interface** - Call from C, C++, and other languages via ArrowSchema, ArrowArray, and ArrowArrayStream
41:- **WASM Compatible** - 103 KB plain, 184 KB with all pure Zig codecs, or 446 KB with C codecs (brotli-compressed)
87:- **Embed directly** - Use Parquet from Zig or through the C ABI instead of shelling out to a separate tool or service
88:- **Keep deployment simple** - Stay native without requiring the JVM, Python, or the full Arrow C++ stack
89:- **Ship across targets** - Use the same core library on desktops, servers, edge devices, serverless workloads, and WASM

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

## [Unreleased]

### Performance
- Streaming row iterator: `DynamicReader.rowIteratorStreaming()` and `rowIteratorStreamingProjected()` return a `StreamingRowIterator` that reuses one row buffer. Contract: the row and its byte slices are valid until the next `next()` or `deinit()`. Memory is bounded by one row group. If loading a row group fails, the next `next()` retries that row group.
- Zero-copy byte arrays on flat reads: PLAIN and dictionary BYTE_ARRAY values (V1 and V2) are slices of the page buffer instead of per-value copies.
- Flat PLAIN fast path for INT32, INT64, FLOAT and DOUBLE pages.
- Word-at-a-time bit unpacking for RLE and bit-packed runs; RLE fill uses memset.
- Flat row assembly without clones: non-nested reads move decoded values into rows, and `rowIterator()` keeps its value block in an iterator arena.
- Write: PLAIN data pages built in one buffer with definition levels written in place; dictionary data pages built in one buffer; accumulator bit packing; dictionary size limit checked inside the loop; statistics computed after the dictionary decision.
- Slicing-by-8 CRC-32 for page checksums on write and on checksum-verified reads.

Benchmark, ReleaseFast, zig-only codecs, 1,000,000 rows, Zig 0.16.0, Ryzen 9 7950X (±10%; see `bench/BASELINE.md`). Speedup over the baseline:

| scenario | write | read (rowIterator) | read_stream vs baseline read |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| int64_plain | 3.8x | 2.5x | 8.5x |
| f64_plain | 3.5x | 2.4x | 7.7x |
| int64_nullable | 3.8x | 2.4x | 7.8x |
| str_dict | 1.4x | 2.8x | 6.2x |
| str_unique | 4.8x | 2.1x | 4.1x |
| mixed5 | 2.7x | 1.7x | 3.9x |

Output bytes are unchanged: file sizes match the baseline in every scenario, and golden-byte tests cover the changed write paths.

### Added
- `Row.values_borrowed` flag (default `false`) for rows whose value block is owned by the producer.
- `StreamingRowIterator` is exported from the package root.
- `make bench` target (zig-only, ReleaseFast; `ROWS=<n>` sets the row count).
- Comparison benchmarks: `make bench-rust` (Rust `parquet` crate) and `make bench-js-browsers` / `make bench-js-workerd` (zig-parquet WASM vs hyparquet and parquet-wasm in Chrome, Firefox and workerd). Results in `bench/COMPARE.md`.
- `ZIG=<path>` on any Makefile target selects the Zig toolchain.

### Changed
- Zig 0.16.0 and 0.17.0 are both supported from one tree, and CI tests both.
- `make fmt` requires a Zig 0.16 toolchain (0.17's `zig fmt` emits 0.17-only builtins).
- `pqi cat` and `pqi head` use the streaming row iterator.
- C codec dependencies are lazy: zig-only builds no longer fetch the C codec archives.

### Fixed
- Bit unpacking overflowed `u5` for bit widths 25-31: the byte count was computed in `u5`. This panicked in Debug builds and gave a wrong byte count in ReleaseFast. Fixed by computing in `usize`.
- Overflow-checked level and bit-pack sizes: `bitPackedSize` returns `error.Overflow`, and V2 level cursor checks are overflow-safe.
- Out-of-memory leaks: footer parsers (`ColumnChunk`, `Statistics`, `RowGroup`, `SchemaElement`, `KeyValue`, `FileMetaData`) free partial allocations; nested assembly frees the partial list item and struct field; dynamic decoders free def/rep levels and page results.
- FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY dictionary pages with BIT_PACKED levels longer than the page panicked; they now return `error.EndOfData`.
- Repeated footer lists (schema, row groups, key/value metadata) leaked the earlier value; they are now freed before replacement.
- `DynamicWriter` (and any `SchemaNode`-built schema) wrote `num_children = <struct field count>` on the repeated `list` group of a `list<struct>` column. Files with such a column followed by other columns failed to read back with `error.InvalidSchema`. The group now has one child, the `element` group.
- GEOMETRY / GEOGRAPHY logical types leaked the `crs` string when parsing failed after it was read, or when the field repeated. `LogicalType.deinit` frees it.
- Byte-array decoders initialized `Optional` slots in place from a fallible copy: on an allocation failure the slot already carried the `.value` tag with an undefined payload, and the cleanup path freed garbage (crashed on Linux). The copy is now made before the slot is written.

## [0.2.0] - 2026-04-07

### Changed
- **Pure Zig compression is now the default.** All five codecs (zstd, gzip, snappy, lz4, brotli) use pure Zig implementations out of the box. C/C++ backends are opt-in via `-Dcodecs=c-only` or individual `c-<codec>` tokens.
- `-Dcodecs=` token rename: Zig codecs are now plain `zstd`, `snappy`, `gzip`, `lz4`, `brotli`; C codecs are `c-zstd`, `c-snappy`, `c-gzip`, `c-lz4`, `c-brotli`
- Removed `-Dprefer-zig` build flag — Zig always wins when compiled in
- Dissolved `compress.experimental` namespace — Zig codec modules are now top-level
- Renamed `stable` codec preset to `c-only`
- Renamed codec source files: `zig_*.zig` → `*.zig`, `*.zig` (C) → `c_*.zig`

### Fixed
- All five Zig decompressors now treat `uncompressed_size` as a capacity hint only; actual decompressed bytes are returned regardless of hint value. Fixes decompression of files with bogus metadata hints (e.g. `large_string_map.brotli.parquet`)
- Brotli decompressor converted to `ArrayListUnmanaged` output — no longer pre-allocates to hint size
- Fixed pre-existing double-free in lz4 decompressor (errdefer + explicit free)
- Fixed `large_file` example: column count check compared physical schema leaves against logical columns (incorrect for nested types)

### Added
- Pure Zig LZ4 raw block codec with cross-implementation testing
- Pure Zig Brotli codec: full RFC 7932 decompressor + quality-0 compressor, with cross-implementation testing
- SortingColumn support: parse, serialize, and expose in writer API
- C→Zig direction added to all five codec cross-implementation round-trip tests
- Oversized hint test added to all five Zig decompressors

## [0.1.6] - 2026-04-04

### Added
- Experimental pure Zig gzip codec (`zig-gzip`) with full deflate encoder and cross-implementation testing
- Level-9 deflate encoder with LZ77 compression, Huffman tree building, and RLE tree descriptor encoding
- Concatenated gzip member support in the zig_gzip decompressor

name: Nightly Fuzz

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 3 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      seconds:
        description: "Mutation-loop seconds per target"
        default: "600"

env:
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: "true"

jobs:
  campaign:
    name: Fuzz ${{ matrix.target }} (nightly)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        target: [ipc-stream, ipc-stream-zero-copy, ipc-file, array-layout, compute, c-abi]
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Set up Zig
        uses: mlugg/setup-zig@v2
        with:
          version: "0.17.0"

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - name: Replay committed corpus
        run: zig build fuzz-corpus

      # ReleaseSafe keeps every safety check (our sanitizer) at several times Debug's speed.
      - name: Mutation campaign
        run: python tools/fuzz.py --optimize ReleaseSafe --out .fuzz-out run --targets ${{ matrix.target }} --seconds ${{ inputs.seconds || '600' }}

      - name: Triage report
        if: always()
        run: python tools/fuzz_triage.py .fuzz-out | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Upload findings and corpus growth
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: fuzz-${{ matrix.target }}
          path: .fuzz-out/${{ matrix.target }}
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      - name: Fail on findings
        run: test ! -e .fuzz-out/${{ matrix.target }}/index.json

  coverage-guided:
    name: std.testing.fuzz (coverage-guided, Linux)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    # Zig's built-in fuzzer is young: informational until it has run green for a while.
    continue-on-error: true
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Set up Zig
        uses: mlugg/setup-zig@v2
        with:
          version: "0.17.0"

      - name: Fuzz every target (iteration-limited, headless)
        run: zig build fuzz-test --fuzz=2M

"Mutation strategies" and "Gaps and recommended research programme" before any task).
Template code: `C:/Users/cable/Documents/dev/zarrow/fuzz/fuzz.zig` and `docs/fuzzing.md` at zarrow
commit e93f5c3. This is the same owner's Arrow library; its harness is dual 0.16/0.17 and CI-proven.
Phase 1 ports its shape, with the targets changed to Parquet ones.

Phases: **1** byte-level fuzz harness (safety oracle, all OSes) → **2** schema-aware round trip and
metamorphic reader/writer cross product → **3** cross-engine differential → **4** depth: ledger,
structure-aware mutation, 32-bit replay. Phases are ordered by bug-finding value per unit of effort.
Each phase ends with a gate and can be reviewed and merged on its own. Phase 1 needs no owner
decision. Decisions D1-D6 (at the end) block only the tasks that name them.

| # | Fact | Evidence |
|---|---|---|

| F3 | OOM sweeps exist: `checkAllAllocationFailures` (column_decoder.zig:3120) and hand-rolled `FailingAllocator` loops (nested.zig:744, footer_parse_test.zig:31/74, roundtrip_test.zig:4829). | grep |

| F5 | Under a plain `zig build test`, a fuzz test runs once per `.corpus` entry and once on empty input. This works on **Windows with both versions**. | `lib/compiler/test_runner.zig` `fuzz()` (0.16 l.526-626). Scratch probe `fzwin/t.zig`: 0.16 and 0.17 both print "2 fuzz tests found", all pass. 0.17 on Windows needs a short `--cache-dir` (MAX_PATH). |
| F6 | `--fuzz` is **not implemented on Windows** (both versions), nor on 32-bit hosts. The fuzzer object formats are ELF and Mach-O only, so it runs on Linux and macOS. | 0.16 `build_runner.zig:836`, 0.17 `Maker.zig:2572` and `Maker/WebServer.zig:278` ("--fuzz not yet implemented for windows"). `fuzzer.zig:185` supports `.elf` and `.macho`. |

ReleaseSafe works. 0.17 fixed this (`writeErrorReturnTrace`, test_runner.zig:587). | WSL probe `~/fzprobe-zp`: `zig build test --fuzz=300K` on Debug gives "expected type '*const debug.StackTrace'". `-Doptimize=ReleaseSafe` runs (300K runs in about 20 s on a trivial target). |

The crashing input goes to `<cache>/f/crash` as the Smith byte stream: for a target that does one `smith.slice()`, that is a u32 LE length followed by the input bytes. ### R2. Zig API gotchas (0.16 and 0.17)

- `std.ArrayList(T)`: `.empty`, and pass the allocator to every method. In-memory output goes to
  `std.Io.Writer.Allocating`.
- Files: `std.Io.Dir.cwd().readFileAlloc(io, path, gpa, .limited(n))`, `openDir(io, p, .{ .iterate = true })`,
  `it.next(io)`. Copy the exact calls from zarrow `fuzz/fuzz.zig` `listInputs` and `replay`; they compile on both versions.
- `std.testing.allocator` and `std.testing.io` are compile errors outside tests. Harness functions
  take `gpa: Allocator` and `io: std.Io`, and only `test` blocks pass the testing ones.
  `std.testing.FailingAllocator` is fine in the exe.
- Executable entry: `pub fn main(init: std.process.Init) !void` (`init.gpa`, `init.io`, `init.arena`,
  `init.minimal.args.toSlice(arena)`).

### R3. Dual-version rules

Use the AGENTS.md table (`@splat`, never `**`; `std.fmt.allocPrint`; `@intFromEnum`/`@enumFromInt`;
`std.heap.DebugAllocator(.{})`; no new `std.meta.fields`/`Int`/`Tag`; `std.meta.stringToEnum` is
fine). No `builtin.zig_version` gates. `make fmt` only with Z16. **Every task proves both versions
the same way:** `make test-lib CODECS=zig-only` with Z16 and with Z17 (the corpus replay is part of
`test`), plus the task's own `make fuzz-run ... ZIG=<both>` line for exe changes.

### R4. Hardening rules apply to harness code too

The harness parses untrusted bytes just as the library does. Never `@intCast` input-derived values;
use `Input.below(n)`, `% n` or `safe.castTo`. Every slice of input goes through `Input.rest()` or a
bounds check. A harness panic is reported as a library bug, so the harness itself must never panic
on input.

### R5. When a target finds something

1. Save the input. The `run` loop leaves it in `zig-parquet/.fuzz-out/<target>/current.bin`;
   `fuzz-cov` leaves it in `<cache>/f/crash` (strip the first 4 bytes: `tail -c +5 crash > input.bin`).
2. Minimize it: `python zig-parquet/fuzz/minimize.py <target> input.bin out.bin` (task 1.8).
3. Report target, kind (panic message / `fuzz-leak` / `fuzz-oom` / `fuzz-hang` / `mismatch`), the first
   `src/` stack frame, and the minimized file. **Do not fix the library in the same task.**
4. Fix tasks (separate, owner-approved) follow zarrow `docs/fuzzing.md` "Fix it": fix at the trust
   boundary in the shared function. Never loosen validation, catch a panic or special-case the input.
   Then promote the input as a regression (R8).
5. If the input is a *valid* Parquet file (another engine reads it) and zig-parquet rejects it, that is a
   compatibility gap, not a fuzz bug. Add it to `test-files-wild/` with a line in
   `expected-failures.txt` and open an issue.

### R6. Stop and ask when

- a test fails and two honest fix attempts did not fix it;
- a change needs a file the task does not list, or a `src/` change (Phase 1-3 tasks touch `src/` only
  where named);
- the compiler shows a 0.16/0.17 difference that R3 does not cover;
- a target produces more than 3 distinct findings in its first 5 minutes (likely a harness bug).

### R7. What NOT to do (whole plan)

- No new Zig dependencies, no fuzzing frameworks, no Python packages beyond `duckdb` (D6).
- No public API changes. Phase 1-3 add nothing to `src/` except task 2.4's internal encoder parameter.
- No changes to library defaults (checksums, dictionary, page size) to make a target pass.
- No rewrites of zarrow code "to be nicer". Port it, rename it, change only what Parquet needs.

### R8. Regression promotion: where findings live (permanent)

| Finding | Lives in | Name | Expected behaviour recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Crash, leak, hang or OOM on some input (any byte target) | `zig-parquet/fuzz/corpus/<target>/` | `regress-<yyyymmdd>-<area>-<slug>.bin` (minimized raw input, not Smith-encoded) | one line in `zig-parquet/fuzz/corpus/expected.txt`: `<target>/<file> ok \| error.<Name> \| error` |
| Wrong values from a valid file | `zig-parquet/src/tests/<area>_test.zig` | `test "regress: <slug>"` that builds the minimized case in code; or a ≤ 4 KiB file in `fuzz/corpus/file/` plus an exact-row assertion | the test itself |
| Writer bug (round trip or interop) | `zig-parquet/src/tests/writer_*_test.zig` | `test "regress: <slug>"`: write the minimized Case, read it back, compare | the test |
| Another engine's bug (xdiff) | `test-files-arrow/xdiff-known.txt` | `<file> <engine> <reason/upstream link>` | that line |

`zig build test` replays every corpus file on every CI lane and both Zig versions, and asserts the
`expected.txt` outcome exactly. Pinning the error name catches error-class drift as well as crashes.

## Phase 1: byte-level harness, safety oracle (about 3-4 Haiku-days)

Goal: every untrusted-input surface gets a target. On every input, the oracle checks that there is
no panic, no leak (per-input count), no live allocation over 256 MiB and no hang over 10 s, and

```zig
//! Shared fuzz helpers.
const std = @import("std");

/// Fuzz decisions read from the input. Exhausted input yields zeros, so a shorter
/// input is always a smaller case: truncating is our shrinker.
pub const Input = struct {
    bytes: []const u8,
    pos: usize = 0,

    pub fn byte(in: *Input) u8 {
        if (in.pos >= in.bytes.len) return 0;
        defer in.pos += 1;
        return in.bytes[in.pos];
    }
    /// In [0, n); 0 when n == 0.
    pub fn below(in: *Input, n: usize) usize {
        if (n == 0) return 0;
        return (@as(usize, in.byte()) | @as(usize, in.byte()) << 8) % n;
    }
    /// Little-endian, zero-padded past the end.
    pub fn int(in: *Input, comptime T: type) T {
        var buf: [@sizeOf(T)]u8 = @splat(0);
        for (&buf) |*b| b.* = in.byte();
        return std.mem.readInt(T, &buf, .little);
    }
    pub fn rest(in: *Input) []const u8 {
        const r = in.bytes[@min(in.pos, in.bytes.len)..];
        in.pos = in.bytes.len;
        return r;
    }
};

/// What one execution looked like; a new `sig` grows the run loop's corpus.
pub const Feedback = struct {
    err: ?anyerror = null,
    rows: u64 = 0,
    detail: u64 = 0, // target-specific bits (encodings seen, reader modes that succeeded, ...)

    pub fn sig(f: Feedback) u64 {
        var h = std.hash.Wyhash.init(0);
        h.update(if (f.err) |e| @errorName(e) else "ok");
        h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&@min(f.rows, 8)));
        h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&f.detail));
        return h.final();
    }
};
```

## Phase 2: schema-aware generation, round trip, metamorphic cross product (about 4-5 days)

Goal: catch the bugs that live in valid files and feature combinations (list<struct>, DELTA cap), which byte
fuzzing cannot see. The oracle is the generated Case itself: what was written must be read back, in every reader
mode, under every writer option.

    int64, float_, double_, bytes, string, date, uuid, json, enum_, bson, float16, interval, timestamp_*, time_*,

## Phase 3: cross-engine differential (about 3-4 days; D1, D6)

Goal: interoperability correctness in both directions. Readers: zig-parquet, PyArrow (Arrow C++), DuckDB (independent C++)
and arrow-rs (independent Rust). Parquity's "no privileged oracle" rule applies: any engine that disagrees with the others
is reported, including zig-parquet. Files under test: `test-files-wild`, `test-files-arrow`, plus N files generated by
the Phase 2 generator (zig as the writer).

Canonical row form (all engines must emit this exactly; JSON Lines, one object per row, keys = top-level columns in schema order):

| Parquet leaf (physical / logical) | canonical JSON value |
|---|---|
| null at any level | `null` (a null list ≠ an empty list `[]`) |
| BOOLEAN | `true` / `false` |
| INT32, INT64 (any INT/DATE/TIME/TIMESTAMP annotation) | decimal **string** of the *physical signed* value (`"-5"`). Unsigned annotations are shown as their signed bit pattern. |
| FLOAT, DOUBLE | `"f32:xxxxxxxx"` / `"f64:xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"` hex of the bits; every NaN → `"nan"` |
| DECIMAL (any physical) | `"dec:<unscaled integer>"` |
| INT96 | `"i96:<24 hex>"` of the 12 stored bytes |
| BYTE_ARRAY, FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY (all other logical types: STRING, ENUM, JSON, BSON, UUID, FLOAT16, INTERVAL, GEOMETRY, GEOGRAPHY) | `"hex:<lowercase hex>"` |
| LIST | array |
| MAP | array of `[key, value]` pairs, in file order |
| STRUCT | object, fields in schema order |

"Written" = the DynamicWriter can produce the cell (the Phase 2 generator must hit it; this is asserted in 2.5). "Read" = seeds
must contain it (ledger 4.1). **R** = required cell, - = not applicable (the feature does not exist in zig-parquet).

## What we are adopting from the research, and what we are not

Adopted: the layered oracle hierarchy (safety → structural via `arrow_check` → semantic round trip → cross-engine → metamorphic
reader modes); separate small targets rather than one giant one; good seeds over engine sophistication (F9); the shared corpus as a
baseline, with minimized findings promoted forever (R8); a Case-based generator with "no privileged oracle" (Parquity's ideas,
without the tool); feature cross-products (2.2, 2.3); a semantic-coverage ledger checked by a test (2.5); a ground-truth benchmark of
real bugs (1.10); resource exhaustion as its own finding class (`fuzz-oom` at 256 MiB live and `fuzz-hang` at 10 s, triaged
separately; wiring `AllocationLimits` into `DynamicReaderOptions` is decision D5); oracles run as untrusted subprocesses.

Not adopted, and why:
- **OSS-Fuzz / libFuzzer / AFL++ / Honggfuzz**: no Zig language support; Zig has only `-ffuzz` for its own runtime; there is no ASan
  for Zig code (F11). The bridge would be an unverified spike with low payoff. Zig safety checks (Debug/ReleaseSafe), plus
  DebugAllocator leak and double-free detection and 0xaa poisoning, are our sanitizer. (D2)
- **FormatFuzzer, FuzzBerg, Parquity as tools**: they belong to C++ or Python ecosystems and would be a heavy integration.
  We take their ideas instead (4.2 is our structure-aware mutator, built on our own Thrift writer).
- **proptest-style shrinking**: replaced by the byte decision stream, where truncating or zeroing bytes yields a smaller Case, and by `minimize.py`.
- **Pairwise / t-wise generators**: exhaustive where the space is small (2.3), random plus a ledger elsewhere. Add pairwise only if the ledger shows persistent holes.
- **20-30 repetition statistical engine benchmark**: overkill here; the ground-truth table uses 3 seeds per bug.
- **Encryption, bloom-filter, async and row-selection-policy dimensions**: zig-parquet has none of them (F16).
- **hyparquet as an oracle**: it converts logical types to JS values (Number, BigInt, Date), which loses exactness for some types, so it would need a third normalizer. `bench/js` keeps its checksum interop matrix as a sanity check. parquet-wasm is arrow-rs (F19), so it adds no independence.
- **Typed `Writer` in the generator**: its types are comptime and cannot be generated at runtime; it shares `column_writer` and schema generation with DynamicWriter, which 2.2 and 2.3 cover. Existing typed tests stay.
- **valgrind**: not installed (F12); consider it for the Linux `file-oom` lane only if a Linux-only crash class recurs.

```zig
//! Shared fuzz helpers.
const std = @import("std");

/// Fuzz decisions read from the input. Exhausted input yields zeros, so a shorter
/// input is always a smaller case: truncating is our shrinker.
pub const Input = struct {
    bytes: []const u8,
    pos: usize = 0,

    pub fn byte(in: *Input) u8 {
        if (in.pos >= in.bytes.len) return 0;
        defer in.pos += 1;
        return in.bytes[in.pos];
    }
    /// In [0, n); 0 when n == 0.
    pub fn below(in: *Input, n: usize) usize {
        if (n == 0) return 0;
        return (@as(usize, in.byte()) | @as(usize, in.byte()) << 8) % n;
    }
    /// Little-endian, zero-padded past the end.
    pub fn int(in: *Input, comptime T: type) T {
        var buf: [@sizeOf(T)]u8 = @splat(0);
        for (&buf) |*b| b.* = in.byte();
        return std.mem.readInt(T, &buf, .little);
    }
    pub fn rest(in: *Input) []const u8 {
        const r = in.bytes[@min(in.pos, in.bytes.len)..];
        in.pos = in.bytes.len;
        return r;
    }
};

/// What one execution looked like; a new `sig` grows the run loop's corpus.
pub const Feedback = struct {
    err: ?anyerror = null,
    rows: u64 = 0,
    detail: u64 = 0, // target-specific bits (encodings seen, reader modes that succeeded, ...)

    pub fn sig(f: Feedback) u64 {
        var h = std.hash.Wyhash.init(0);
        h.update(if (f.err) |e| @errorName(e) else "ok");
        h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&@min(f.rows, 8)));
        h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&f.detail));
        return h.final();
    }
};
```

## Phase 2: schema-aware generation, round trip, metamorphic cross product (about 4-5 days)

Goal: catch the bugs that live in valid files and feature combinations (list<struct>, DELTA cap), which byte
fuzzing cannot see. The oracle is the generated Case itself: what was written must be read back, in every reader
mode, under every writer option.

### Task 2.1 Case generator

- Files: new `zig-parquet/fuzz/case.zig`
- Depends on: Gate 1
- **Model: Sonnet or Opus**
- Change: `pub fn generate(in: *common.Input, arena: Allocator) !Case`, where `Case = { columns: []ColumnSpec, rows: [][]Value, opts: WriterOpts }`.
  - Columns: `1 + below(6)`. A leaf type comes from the TypeInfo presets (dynamic_writer.zig l.79-125: bool_, int32,
    int64, float_, double_, bytes, string, date, uuid, json, enum_, bson, float16, interval, timestamp_*, time_*,
    int8…uint64, `forDecimal(p, s)` with p in {5, 18, 30}, `fixedBytes(1 + below(16))`), optional with

    **Bias:** put a nested column before at least one other column in half of the cases (the 9cdfe67 shape).

- Files: new `zig-parquet/fuzz/t_roundtrip.zig`; `fuzz.zig` (add `.roundtrip` to `Target`, dispatch and test; `adaptSeed` returns null)
- Depends on: 2.1
- Change: generate → write → `openBufferDynamic` (checksum validation on when the case wrote checksums) → check:
  1. `readAllRows` over all row groups == `case.rows` (`valuesEqual`), and `getTotalNumRows()` == the row count.

## Phase 3: cross-engine differential (about 3-4 days; D1, D6)

Goal: interoperability correctness in both directions. Readers: zig-parquet, PyArrow (Arrow C++), DuckDB (independent C++)
and arrow-rs (independent Rust). Parquity's "no privileged oracle" rule applies: any engine that disagrees with the others
is reported, including zig-parquet. Files under test: `test-files-wild`, `test-files-arrow`, plus N files generated by
the Phase 2 generator (zig as the writer).

Canonical row form (all engines must emit this exactly; JSON Lines, one object per row, keys = top-level columns in schema order):

| Parquet leaf (physical / logical) | canonical JSON value |
|---|---|
| null at any level | `null` (a null list ≠ an empty list `[]`) |
| BOOLEAN | `true` / `false` |
| INT32, INT64 (any INT/DATE/TIME/TIMESTAMP annotation) | decimal **string** of the *physical signed* value (`"-5"`). Unsigned annotations are shown as their signed bit pattern. |
| FLOAT, DOUBLE | `"f32:xxxxxxxx"` / `"f64:xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"` hex of the bits; every NaN → `"nan"` |
| DECIMAL (any physical) | `"dec:<unscaled integer>"` |
| INT96 | `"i96:<24 hex>"` of the 12 stored bytes |
| BYTE_ARRAY, FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY (all other logical types: STRING, ENUM, JSON, BSON, UUID, FLOAT16, INTERVAL, GEOMETRY, GEOGRAPHY) | `"hex:<lowercase hex>"` |
| LIST | array |
| MAP | array of `[key, value]` pairs, in file order |
| STRUCT | object, fields in schema order |

## Semantic-coverage matrix (zig-parquet's real feature set)

"Written" = the DynamicWriter can produce the cell (the Phase 2 generator must hit it; this is asserted in 2.5). "Read" = seeds
must contain it (ledger 4.1). **R** = required cell, - = not applicable (the feature does not exist in zig-parquet).

| Dimension | Values | Written | Read | Measured by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Physical type | BOOLEAN, INT32, INT64, INT96, FLOAT, DOUBLE, BYTE_ARRAY, FLBA | R except INT96 | R all | case counters; ledger |
| Logical type | none, STRING, ENUM, JSON, BSON, UUID, DATE, TIME ms/us/ns, TIMESTAMP ms/us/ns (utc and local), DECIMAL on int32/int64/FLBA/BYTE_ARRAY, INT 8/16/32/64 signed and unsigned, FLOAT16, INTERVAL, GEOMETRY, GEOGRAPHY | R (presets) | R | case counters; ledger |
| Value encoding × physical | PLAIN all; RLE_DICTIONARY / PLAIN_DICTIONARY all but bool; RLE bool; DELTA_BINARY_PACKED int32/64; DELTA_LENGTH_BYTE_ARRAY and DELTA_BYTE_ARRAY byte arrays; BYTE_STREAM_SPLIT int32/int64/float/double (+FLBA read) | R for the writer's set (F16) | R all | case counters; ledger; `page`/`spec` targets for the rest |
| Level encoding | RLE, BIT_PACKED (deprecated, read only) | RLE | R both | ledger; `page` recipe |
| Page version | V1, V2 (incl. `is_compressed = false`) | V1 only | R both | ledger; `spec` (V2 page) and `rewrite` (V2 flag) |
| Codec × dictionary | {none, snappy, gzip, lz4_raw, zstd, brotli} × {dict, no dict}; LZ4 (hadoop) and LZO rejected by design | R | R | case counters; ledger |
| Repetition × nesting depth | required/optional/repeated × depth 0-3; list, struct, map; nested **followed by** another column | R | R | case counters |
| Null pattern | 0%, 5%, 50%, 100%, single null, long runs | R | - | case counters |
| Row group / page shape | 1 vs many row groups; tiny pages (64 B); page boundary inside a list; dictionary fallback (size limit) | R | R | case counters; ledger (page counts from the offset index) |
| Page index | absent / present; `readRowsFiltered` with empty and range filters | R | R | case counters |
| Checksums | written on/off × validated on/off × corrupt | R (on/off) | R (two corrupt files in wild) | case counters; `file` target bit |
| Reader mode | readAllRows, rowIterator, rowIteratorStreaming, projected (both), readRowsFiltered, Arrow bridge, C ABI stream | - | R | `Feedback.detail` bits in file/roundtrip/arrow |
| Not applicable | bloom filters, encryption, async reader, row-selection policies, VARIANT (parquet-testing `variant/`, not supported) | - | - | excluded by design |

Code coverage is coarse and complementary: the `--fuzz=N` report prints `Coverage: x/y` PCs per target, and nightly records it.
No line-coverage tool is adopted (kcov would work on Linux; add it only if the ledger and the PC counts disagree).

## What we are adopting from the research, and what we are not

Adopted: the layered oracle hierarchy (safety → structural via `arrow_check` → semantic round trip → cross-engine → metamorphic
reader modes); separate small targets rather than one giant one; good seeds over engine sophistication (F9); the shared corpus as a
baseline, with minimized findings promoted forever (R8); a Case-based generator with "no privileged oracle" (Parquity's ideas,
without the tool); feature cross-products (2.2, 2.3); a semantic-coverage ledger checked by a test (2.5); a ground-truth benchmark of
real bugs (1.10); resource exhaustion as its own finding class (`fuzz-oom` at 256 MiB live and `fuzz-hang` at 10 s, triaged
separately; wiring `AllocationLimits` into `DynamicReaderOptions` is decision D5); oracles run as untrusted subprocesses.

Not adopted, and why:
- **OSS-Fuzz / libFuzzer / AFL++ / Honggfuzz**: no Zig language support; Zig has only `-ffuzz` for its own runtime; there is no ASan
  for Zig code (F11). The bridge would be an unverified spike with low payoff. Zig safety checks (Debug/ReleaseSafe), plus
  DebugAllocator leak and double-free detection and 0xaa poisoning, are our sanitizer. (D2)
- **FormatFuzzer, FuzzBerg, Parquity as tools**: they belong to C++ or Python ecosystems and would be a heavy integration.
  We take their ideas instead (4.2 is our structure-aware mutator, built on our own Thrift writer).
- **proptest-style shrinking**: replaced by the byte decision stream, where truncating or zeroing bytes yields a smaller Case, and by `minimize.py`.
- **Pairwise / t-wise generators**: exhaustive where the space is small (2.3), random plus a ledger elsewhere. Add pairwise only if the ledger shows persistent holes.
- **20-30 repetition statistical engine benchmark**: overkill here; the ground-truth table uses 3 seeds per bug.
- **Encryption, bloom-filter, async and row-selection-policy dimensions**: zig-parquet has none of them (F16).
- **hyparquet as an oracle**: it converts logical types to JS values (Number, BigInt, Date), which loses exactness for some types, so it would need a third normalizer. `bench/js` keeps its checksum interop matrix as a sanity check. parquet-wasm is arrow-rs (F19), so it adds no independence.
- **Typed `Writer` in the generator**: its types are comptime and cannot be generated at runtime; it shares `column_writer` and schema generation with DynamicWriter, which 2.2 and 2.3 cover. Existing typed tests stay.
- **valgrind**: not installed (F12); consider it for the Linux `file-oom` lane only if a Linux-only crash class recurs.

---

| # | Decision | Blocks | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Add parquet-java (JVM) as a fourth reader | 3.x (optional task) | **Not now.** Phase 3 already has three independent families (Arrow C++, DuckDB, arrow-rs). Revisit after Gate 3 as a **CI-only** nightly job (`actions/setup-java`, no local JVM) that reads **zig-written files only**, because parquet-mr consumers (Spark, Trino) are where page-index interop bugs showed up (the research note's zero-rows issue) and zig writes page indexes. |
| D2 | Apply to OSS-Fuzz | none | **No.** No Zig support; acceptance favours widely deployed projects; the in-house nightly gives the same signal for this codebase. |
| D3 | Scheduled CI minutes | 1.9 nightly | **Yes, nightly, about 90 runner-min (+10 for xdiff from Phase 3).** Free on a public repo. Scheduled workflows on a fork must be enabled once in the Actions tab of `Gewelf-Labs/zig-parquet`. |
| D4 | Vendor `apache/parquet-testing` | none | It **is already vendored** as a Feb 2026 snapshot (F15). Keep the snapshot (no submodule). Refresh it **once** now to pick up newer `bad_data/` reproducers, re-run `make validate-wild`, and update `expected-failures.txt`. |
